paragraphs: Rabbi Shasha, son of Rabbi Abba. (Shashai; [Ezra 10:40](https://www.sefaria.org/Ezra.10.40).)[^1]

He is mentioned at the beginning of [Shemot Rabbah, chapter 24](https://www.sefaria.org/Shemot_Rabbah.24.1): he would write the he below and the lamed above, in the word הלה׳ in the phrase “Is this how you repay the Lord?” Yuḥasin has the reading “bar Rava.” But the source of the midrash is the Yerushalmi, [Megillah, chapter 1, halakhah 9](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Megillah.1.9.10), where the reading is “R' Yosha, son of Rav Chanael.” The Yerushalmi’s reading is the correct one, as Rav Chanael too is known to have been a scribe.[^2]

notes.text: The discussion concerns the graphic arrangement of the initial he and lamed in הלה׳ in [Deuteronomy 32:6](https://www.sefaria.org/Deuteronomy.32.6).

Shemot Rabbah reads Shesha son of Rabbi Abba. The Yerushalmi reads “Rav Shesh’a son of Rav Chananel,” whereas Hyman quotes “Yosha, son of Rav Chanael.” The preference for the Yerushalmi is Hyman’s textual judgment.
